verdict.line: You lose if you walk into his Seismic Shard poke range before level 3 or stand in Ground Slam's attack-speed slow mid-trade; you win if you pull him with E the instant his Ground Slam is down and stack Hemorrhage to five before he can reset the fight.

brief.thesis: This is a stack race, not a burst matchup: Malphite has no hard CC or burst before level 6, just Seismic Shard poke and a shield that recharges if he avoids damage, while Darius needs sustained contact to ramp Hemorrhage to five stacks for the enrage and a true-damage Guillotine. Whoever controls when the fight starts wins it, which lines up with the dead-even 50.5% win rate across 97 games.

theirWindow.when: Granite Shield charged and E up
theirWindow.what: If he hasn't been hit recently his passive shield is sitting full and absorbs your opener cold, and Ground Slam's attack-speed reduction stretches out how long it takes you to stack Hemorrhage. Throw one auto or a Q handle hit from range first to pop the shield before you commit your real combo.

yourWindow.when: His E (Ground Slam) is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: This is your entire trade window: no attack-speed slow waiting and no armor-scaled magic damage ready, so land E (Apprehend) to pull him into range and start stacking Hemorrhage freely. It's a 7-second cooldown, so it comes around constantly.

powerCurve.note: His Q outranges your entire kit
E unlocks forced pulls he can't escape
Guillotine true damage plus first item spike
His armor stacking offsets your damage

start.why: It's the higher-win-rate start in this matchup (56.9% over 58 games vs. 47.1% for Doran's Shield) because this lane is decided by who converts a forced all-in, not by soaking passive poke damage — Malphite's only ranged tool is a single-target Seismic Shard, not AoE harass.

boots.why: Every point of his kit (Seismic Shard, Brutal Strikes, Ground Slam, Unstoppable Force) is magic damage, and the tenacity cuts down the slow from his Q and the stun window after his R knockup.

core.why: The active haste closes the gap faster than his Q slow can stretch it, and the lethality punches through the bonus armor he gets from activating Brutal Strikes.
Stacked move speed lets you run him down before he can kite with Seismic Shard, and the HP buffers the Ground Slam + Unstoppable Force combo.
Converts the burst from his engage into delayed damage that your Hemorrhage ticks and Q healing can outheal, which is the whole point in a stack-race matchup like this.

situational.when: you're ahead and want the burst-and-slow all-in path instead of Youmuu's
he's chaining Unstoppable Force into Ground Slam and you need the shield to survive the engage
their comp leans magic damage and Treads alone aren't covering it
you'd rather outrun Seismic Shard and his R charge than tank through them

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacks over the course of the extended trade this matchup demands, and the healing conversion pairs with Hemorrhage and Q lifesteal to win the drawn-out fight his Granite Shield is trying to force. Master-tier Darius players instead run Stormraider's Surge (Sorcery) across 671 games — that suits a more kiting, pick-based playstyle that leans on the speed burst to land E (Apprehend) rather than grinding out a stand-and-trade.

summoners.why: Ghost closes the distance his Seismic Shard slow tries to create and helps you stick through Unstoppable Force positioning. Flash+Ignite (55% over a smaller sample) is the higher-win-rate alternative if you want to guarantee kills once he's capped at five Hemorrhage stacks.

playing.title: Punish his E cooldown
playing.detail: Only commit to a real trade when his E (Ground Slam) is down. Outside that window his attack-speed slow drags out your stacking and his passive magic nuke adds up fast.

playing.title: Pull through his Q poke
playing.detail: If he opens from range with Q (Seismic Shard, 8s cooldown, steals your move speed), don't walk up into it — fire E (Apprehend) immediately to erase the range gap and start your combo on your terms.

playing.title: Pop Granite Shield before committing
playing.detail: His passive shield recharges if he hasn't been hit recently. A single cheap auto or Q handle hit burns it down so your real combo isn't absorbed.

playing.title: Chain Q into W into E
playing.detail: Decimate for the wide hit, Crippling Strike for the slow, Apprehend to keep him locked down — this stacks Hemorrhage fastest and he has no dash to escape it, only the Ground Slam attack-speed debuff.

playing.title: Execute at five stacks
playing.detail: At max Hemorrhage you enrage for bonus AD, and from level 6 R (Noxian Guillotine) deals true damage scaled by those stacks — that ignores whatever armor he's stacked from Brutal Strikes or items.

playing.title: Respect his R range after level 6
playing.detail: Unstoppable Force charges up to 1000 range and knocks up on landing, well outside your own E's 535 range. Don't overextend past your minion wave once it's off cooldown.

playing.title: Hold through his Brutal Strikes window
playing.detail: When he activates W his armor and AD spike for a few seconds. Back off auto-trades during that window rather than feeding stacks into his buffed damage.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/pick-rate numbers above are measured from live OP.GG data on the current patch; the tactical reasoning (cooldown windows, shield timing, trade order) is this brief's own analysis built to explain those numbers, not a separate data source.

stats.opponentTip: Fight Malphite whenever his (E) is on cooldown. If he closes in to use (Q), pull him with [E] to close in on him and deal damage.
